activities.anchor: Scrub through one full revolution below
activities.caption: pair each family with its manufacture
activities.name: rcFamilyMatch

config.prompt: Three classes, three states of the loop — pair each with what makes it:

pairs.right: frozen magma — cooling speed writes the texture
older rock transformed in the solid state by heat and pressure

config.why: Every rock is a stage, not a species — the same atoms pass through all three families over and over.

activities.anchor: a shale can skip the sediment stage entirely
activities.caption: walk a granite's biography
activities.name: rcBiographyBranch

config.root: A granite sits on the coast, hammered by waves. The plates will decide its biography — walk one route.

start.text: Uplift exposes it further; frost and roots pry it apart.

choices.label: The grains travel to the sea and settle
choices.feedback: Weathering to sediment — the surface arc begins.

choices.label: The coast subsides and the granite is dragged toward a mountain-belt root
choices.feedback: The shortcut: no sedimentary holiday, straight to the squeeze.

bury.text: Layer upon layer buries the sand; pressure compacts, minerals cement.

choices.label: It hardens to sandstone and is uplifted again
choices.feedback: A two-class biography — and the round-trip version of the loop.

choices.label: Burial keeps deepening, past where sandstone survives
choices.feedback: Deeper and hotter — the same material, next state.

squeeze.text: Heat climbs with depth and the squeeze is directional — but the rock stays solid.

choices.label: New minerals grow in the solid state: gneiss
choices.feedback: Solid-state cooking — the moment it melts, the story changes class.

choices.label: Deeper still, it crosses the melting line
choices.feedback: The strictest rule: melting evicts a rock from the metamorphic club — it re-enters as magma.

squeeze2.text: Mountain-building or a sinking plate supplies the heat and directional squeeze — never quite enough to melt.

done.text: Granite to sand to sandstone: no shortcuts, no set stations — the road network, not the ferris wheel.

done2.text: The same atoms, a third family: the biography is whatever path the plates happened to drive it along.

melt.text: Back to the forge — and every path begins again from magma.

config.why: Any rock can be melted back to magma, weathered to sediment, or metamorphosed in place — and each outcome can itself be revisited.

activities.anchor: a rare machine driven simultaneously from below and above
activities.caption: file each process by its engine
activities.name: rcEngineSort

config.prompt: Two mismatched engines power the loop — file each process:

items.label: subduction dragging crust toward the melting zone
frost freezing and thawing in a crack
a river carrying grains to the sea
a collision uplifting a mountain belt
evaporation powering the rain that weathers rock

config.why: Half geology, half solar power — the conveyor (plate tectonics) is organised by the heat engine, the surface arc runs on sunlight.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — igneous textures
activities.name: rcIgneousSpot

config.prompt: One of these igneous-texture claims is backwards — click it:
lines: Igneous rocks are hard, crystalline and unlayered.
Slow deep cooling lets crystals grow large enough to see — granite.
Erupted lava freezes so fast the crystals stay microscopic — basalt.
Cooling speed does not matter; chemistry alone sets the crystal size.
Quench instantly and you get obsidian, a natural glass.
config.correction: Cooling speed is the whole story — the same magma makes coarse granite or fine basalt depending only on how fast it loses heat.
config.why: Texture confesses the cooling history: coarse means intrusive and slow, fine means erupted, glassy means quenched.

activities.anchor: shale was compacted mud on a quiet seafloor
activities.caption: true or false — the sedimentary archive
activities.name: rcSedJudge

statements.s: Sandstone was once sand — a river bed, a beach, a desert dune.
statements.why: The layering records the environment of deposition.

statements.s: Coal, oil and gas can form in any rock family.
statements.why: They occur only in sedimentary basins — fossil fuels are buried organic matter, and burial means sediment.

statements.s: The white cliffs of Dover are chalk built of marine algae plates.
statements.why: Uncountable plates, compacted — an archive of surface history.

statements.s: Sediments pile up from the top down, so layers record environment from the surface first.
statements.why: They pile from the bottom: lower layers are older, and the sequence records time and environment.

activities.anchor: hot enough to rearrange atoms, not hot enough to melt
activities.caption: call the crust's heat climb
activities.name: rcGradientEst

config.prompt: Metamorphism works between sedimentation and melting — roughly how fast does temperature climb with depth in the crust?
config.why: About 25–30 °C per kilometre — at a few km down, clay minerals become unstable and rebuild into micas, all while the rock stays solid.
config.context: Pressure grows with the weight above; new, denser minerals form in sequence as both rise.

activities.anchor: At low grades the alignment is a fine
activities.caption: foliation vs lineation — drag the divider
activities.name: rcFabricCompare

config.prompt: Two fabrics, one squeeze — drag between them:

before.label: Foliation — the planar fabric
before.text: Platy minerals orient perpendicular to the maximum compression, like cards fanned flat: slate splits into roofing sheets along it, schist glitters, gneiss segregates into stripes.

after.label: Lineation — the companion fabric
after.text: Elongate minerals or stretched pebbles aligned like grain in wood — recording the direction the material flowed.

config.why: Together they tell a geologist how hot, how squeezed — and which way the squeeze came from.

config.prompt: Grade read from index minerals — put Barrow's zones in order of rising intensity:
items: Chlorite — the lowest grades, barely transformed
Kyanite and sillimanite — near the melting ceiling
config.why: Find garnet and you are in moderate grade; find sillimanite and the rock has stood on magma's doorstep — index minerals are the thermometers of metamorphism.
